main_text.p: idem & AlFiranzabadius. ab iisdem etiam سعير Soairum nomen Idoli fuisse discimus, quod Sairum, nomine aliàs ignem denotante, vocat AlJauharius, ac-tribui Anza peculiare fuisse refert, quam sententiam Poëtæ nescio cujus authoritate confirmans, hoc ipsius dictum laudat.
v. AlJauhar.in سعر [?]in عوض [?]in مور [?]حلفت بمايراث [?] حول عوض [?] وادصاب ترسكر [?] أدي سعير [?]

p.i: Juravi per sanguinem fluentem circa Audum, Et per statuas quas reliquerunt apud Assairum.

main_text.p: ubi & alterius Idoli nomen occurrit, عوض Audi sc. saeculo (testantibus eodem & AlFiranzabadio) cognomi-nis, quod apud tribum Beer Wayeli posteros sa-crum. انصاب [?] autem in dicto Poetæ vel statuas red-dere licet, vel hoc loco, potiùs lapides circa [illegible, ~6 letters] positos, super quibus maclabantur victimæ. Utrumque enim denotare vocem, docet nos AlFiranzabadius, qui cùm نصب [?] esse dixisset, quicquid pro Deo colendum erigitur, scil. Idolum, Statuam, addit & انصاب [?] fuisse lapides circa Caabam positos super quibus sacrificarent لغير الله تعالى [?] i.e. aliis quam Deo altis-simo. Clariùs adhuc Safioddinus النصب الاصنام [?] المنصوبة للعبادة وحجارة كانوا انتصبوها يذبحون عليها للاصنام [?] i.e. Alnosb significat Statuas positas ad cultum, item lapides quos posuerant ut super ipsis sacrificia mactarent Idolis. inde dictum cujusdam sanguine se perfusum autumantis, كاثي نصب احمر [?] i.e. ut si essem lapis rubens, explicat Ebnol Athir, كالنصب الاحمر بدم الذباتج [?] i.e. instar lapidis rubentis sanguine victimarum. quo dicto vel ad lapides super

page.notes: Arabic text is set in a small, worn type; the Arabic words are read with low confidence and are marked [?] throughout, especially the verse lines and the words in the margin. One word in the Arabic phrase after "circa" is not legible and is marked as illegible. The Arabic "نصب" and "انصاب" forms could be misread. Long s is transcribed as s (e.g. "sanguinem", "altissimo"). The "Digitized by Google" stamp at the lower right is excluded. The word "super" at lower right is treated as a catchword and is not in the text.
